title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يشارك في مؤتمر "نحو تجديد الفقه السياسي الإسلامي" بتونس
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in the Conference "Towards a Renewal of Islamic Political Jurisprudence" in Tunisia
body_ar: يقوم فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو عضو مجلس الأمناء ورئيس لجنة العضوية في الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين ضمن وفد من الاتحاد برئاسة سماحة الشيخ العلامة يوسف القرضاوي رئيس الاتحاد وعضوية علماء من الاتحاد بزيارة إلى تونس في الفترة ما بين الخميس 03 مايو 2012 إلى يوم الثلاثاء 08 مايو الجاري. وحسب البرنامج المعد للزيارة سوف يقوم الوفد بجولة في معظم المدن التونسية كما يشارك الوفد أيضا في مؤتمر "نحو تجديد الفقه السياسي الإسلامي" الذي سينعقد في العاصمة تونس أيام 6 و7 و8 مايو، حيث سيلقي أعضاء الوفد من العلماء والمشايخ عددا من المحاضرات وخطب الجمعة. هذا وكان الشيخ قد ألقى محاضرة في الجامع الكبير بمدينة مساكن تحت عنوان : "ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة" لمتابعة المحاضرة اضغط هنا:
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew — member of the board of trustees and chairman of the membership committee of the International Union of Muslim Scholars — is making a visit to Tunisia as part of a delegation from the Union headed by the eminent scholar Sheikh Yusuf al-Qaradawi, the Union's president, with scholars of the Union as its members, in the period from Thursday 3 May 2012 to Tuesday 8 May of the present month.

According to the programme drawn up for the visit, the delegation will make a tour of most of the Tunisian cities, and will also take part in the conference "Towards a Renewal of Islamic Political Jurisprudence", to be convened in the capital, Tunis, on 6, 7 and 8 May, at which the scholars and sheikhs of the delegation will deliver a number of lectures and Friday sermons.

The Sheikh had also delivered a lecture at the Great Mosque in the city of Msaken under the title "Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and fair exhortation".

*[Site link: "To follow the lecture, click here:"]*

flags.context: the conference title; the record gives no content from it
flags.note: The record establishes that the Sheikh attended a conference on renewing Islamic political jurisprudence, in Tunis, one year after the Tunisian revolution, in a delegation headed by Yusuf al-Qaradawi. It contains not one word of what he said there. Given the subject and the moment, a reader will expect substance and find an itinerary; nothing may be supplied. 'الفقه السياسي' is rendered 'political jurisprudence' rather than 'political thought', since fiqh is the technical discipline and the conference title is about renewing it.

flags.arabic: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة
flags.context: the title of the Sheikh's lecture at the Great Mosque of Msaken
options: Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and fair exhortation (Sūrat al-Naḥl 16:125)
Invite to the path of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction
flags.note: Sūrat al-Naḥl 16:125, used as a lecture title. The source gives it in ordinary quotation marks with no reference, and the English keeps that form rather than applying the curly-brace citation convention of style guide section 4 to a title. الحكمة is rendered 'wisdom' here rather than the glossary's 'underlying wisdom', which is the technical usul sense and wrong for a Qur'anic imperative. Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

A town in the Sousse Governorate of Tunisia. 'Msaken' is the usual English and French spelling; the Arabic word also means 'dwellings', which is how a machine reading would take it. Recorded because Tunisian and Mauritanian place names recur through this news section and the corpus will need one spelling each.

translator_notes: A news-desk announcement of a forthcoming visit, written on its second day. No content from the Sheikh.
The CMS timestamp, 4 May 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the visit it announces ran 3–8 May 2012.

'سماحة' and 'فضيلة' are both honorifics of address for scholars and have no settled English equivalents; both are rendered by 'the eminent scholar' or dropped where English will not carry them, and neither is inflated into a title.
